text: The Poincaré–Birkhoff–Witt (PBW) theorem states that a $k$-basis of $\mathcal{U}(\mathfrak{g})$ is given by:
choices: the ordered monomials $x_1^{k_1}\cdots x_n^{k_n}$ in a fixed ordered basis of $\mathfrak{g}$
explanation: PBW says the ordered products $x_1^{k_1}\cdots x_n^{k_n}$ (each $k_i \geq 0$) form a basis of $\mathcal{U}(\mathfrak{g})$. The elements of $\mathfrak{g}$ span only degree $\leq 1$; commutators are absorbed by the defining relations; and exterior monomials describe $\Lambda\mathfrak{g}$, whereas $\mathrm{gr}\,\mathcal{U}(\mathfrak{g}) \cong \mathrm{Sym}(\mathfrak{g})$.
